page: Amazon Web Services r7a.medium is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and AMD EPYC 9R14 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the server provides 1 dedicated vCPU mapped to a single physical core running at 3.7 GHz, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 4 MB of L3 cache. Memory configuration includes 8.0 GB of 5 GHz DDR5 RAM, delivering the 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio defining the R7a family. The configuration does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong single-thread computational capacity contrasted against constraints inherent to a single-core design. In single-core tests, the r7a.medium places in the top quartile for stress-ng and Geekbench, reinforced by hardware support for AVX-512 vector instructions and cryptographic acceleration. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression also exhibits upper-tier execution rates. Conversely, multi-core metrics, PassMark scores, and static web serving throughput register in the bottom quartiles due to the presence of only one execution thread. Uncached large-block memory write speeds perform within median ranges, while small-block cached read throughput remains lower.

Qualitatively, the r7a.medium offers a cost-effective path to modern DDR5 memory and current-generation AMD EPYC architecture without requiring the provisioning of excess compute cores. The architectural tradeoff is strict compute concurrency limitation, making it ineffective for parallelized workloads or high-volume simultaneous connection handling. It is best suited for small in-memory key-value stores, lightweight background ETL jobs, low-traffic microservices, and development environments that require an 8 GB memory footprint under modest single-thread demands.
description: Amazon Web Services r7a.medium is an entry-tier memory-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AMD EPYC 9R14 processors. Configured on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 1 dedicated vCPU mapped to a single physical core running at 3.7 GHz, complemented by 8.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory at 5 GHz. The instance does not include bundled local storage or discrete GPU acceleration. Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-thread computational capacity, with top-tier results in single-core stress-ng, Geekbench, and bzip3 decompression tests, enabled by AVX-512 and cryptographic extensions. However, overall multi-core and database operational throughput remain strictly bounded by the single-thread allocation. The r7a.medium offers qualitative cost efficiency by granting low-overhead access to modern DDR5 memory and EPYC processing power without excess compute capacity. It is primarily suited for lightweight in-memory caching, single-threaded background jobs, microservices, and memory-dependent testing workloads.
